tools.name: search_components
tools.description:
Find motors, propellers or batteries in the ThrustLab database.

`component_type` is "motor", "propeller" or "battery". `query` is a
case-insensitive substring of the part name or its maker ("APC", "T-Motor",
"13x6.5"). The maker sits under `spec.brand` for motors and batteries and under
`spec.type`

tools.name: get_component
tools.description:
Read one database row by its id (`comp_…`), with provenance.

    Propeller rows give diameter, pitch, blade count, weight and maximum rpm.
    Blade station geometry is never returned.

tools.name: estimate_propeller

tools.description:

tools.name: get_result
tools.description:
Read a stored result: a share `token` from a run, or a `simulation_id`.

    `simulation_id` needs a ThrustLab API key in `Authorization: Bearer` and
    reads only that account's own runs.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "get_result" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: simulate_powertrain, sweep_powertrain · Private data: search_components, get_component, get_result · Public sink: simulate_powertrain, sweep_powertrain, get_result · Destructive: get_result.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: simulate_powertrain, sweep_powertrain · Private data: search_components, get_component, get_result · Public sink: simulate_powertrain, sweep_powertrain, get_result · Destructive: get_result

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
